ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, signatories and corporate entities against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Egypt's domestic terrorism/terrorist-entity list maintained under Law No. 80 of 2002, OFAC SDN/Sanctions List, Her Majesty's Treasury/European Union consolidated lists, and World Bank sanctioned-firm registers. Domestic and foreign PEPs must receive enhanced due diligence and senior management approval. Any exact-name match, date-of-birth match, or ambiguous ownership chain must be cleared by written legal analysis before incorporation; unresolved matches block GAFI registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI online Investment and Commercial Registration Portal with integrated name reservation service (www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be written in Arabic or Arabic transliteration of the proposed foreign name. Latin-script trade names may be recorded only as a secondary name or brand name. The legal-form suffix 'LLC' or its Arabic equivalent must appear in the name. Arabic transliterations must follow GAFI's official transliteration table and must be clearly distinguishable from all existing Arabic and Latin names in the Commercial Registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank - requires Central Bank of Egypt license
Insurance / Takaful - requires Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority license
Securities / Clearing / Exchange - requires Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority license
Islamic - requires prior approval of religious and regulatory authorities and may only be used for Sharia-compliant businesses
Egypt / Arab Republic of Egypt - restricted official state designation requiring prior ministerial authorisation
President / Government / Ministry / State - prohibited company name elements
Military / Army / Police / National Security - prohibited and summarily rejected
National / Central / Sovereign - sensitive tokens requiring written justification if used in the proposed name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name lapses automatically after 30 calendar days; one extension of 30 days may be requested before expiry by filing a renewal request with GAFI and paying the renewal fee. Upon rejection, GAFI issues a written decision stating the grounds of refusal. The applicant may submit a written grievance to the GAFI Investor Services and Complaints Unit within 15 working days, accompanied by the original reservation receipt, corrected name proposal, and supporting justifications. An internal committee must issue its reconsideration decision within 7 working days. If the name remains refused, the applicant may file an action before Egypt's administrative court (State Council) within 60 days of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole registered office of the LLC. A physical office address in Egypt, evidenced by a lease agreement or title deed, is mandatory for service of process, statutory books, and tax/civil registration. A virtual address may be used only as an additional correspondence address. For the 500-kV gas-insulated switchgear installation business, GAFI and the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company licensing authorities require a fixed Egyptian operating/administrative office and designate Egyptian management in charge of project delivery.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 18 months after incorporation, reflecting mandatory commercial-registry visits, tax office verification, labor/social insurance inspections, and Egyptian Electricity Holding Company technical safety visits for licensed high-voltage electrical contractors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, Articles 45-63 (Limited Liability Company formation and management), as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 12; Commercial Registry requirements under Law No. 34/1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Services Center / Cairo Companies Registry, Ministry of Investment and Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (constitutive instrument) in Arabic submitted through GAFI One-Stop-Shop, together with the statutory Formation Request Form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC under Law No. 159 of 1981; however, the electrical contractor licensing authority may impose a capital threshold. Any declared share capital must be deposited in a blocked temporary Egyptian bank escrow account before commercial registration and is released after issuance of the GAFI incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of [Company Name] LLC be approved under Law No. 159/1981. The subscription of all issued quota/shares by the initial shareholders is ratified. The registered office is fixed at [address], Egypt. The deposited share capital in [Bank Name] and its escrow release are approved. [Name] is appointed as General Manager and legal representative; [Name] is appointed as Financial Officer. They are jointly and severally authorised to complete GAFI registration, sign commercial registration applications, open bank accounts, and file tax registration. All actions prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and ISIC activity pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (in person at One-Stop-Shop or online via GAFI e-Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the GAFI electronic portal, select 'New Company Establishment', choose LLC, enter at least three alternative Arabic company names, select ISIC activity 4321, upload shareholder identity documents, and submit for preliminary approval. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a certificate valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all natural-person shareholders (passport/national ID)
Proposed corporate names in Arabic with transliteration
Declaration of business activity and ISIC code selection
Power of attorney if an attorney-in-fact submits on behalf of shareholders
Foreign ownership pre-clearance questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or similarity, submit a replacement name list in the same GAFI window without a new fee; GAFI will issue a fresh reservation within 24 hours. If the activity is flagged, file a written clarification referencing ISIC 4321 under Law No. 159/1981.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution and notarisation of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI corporate counsels and licensed Egyptian notary public; GAFI legal review for filing purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic LLC constitutive document specifying shareholders, capital, business purpose and manager appointments. All quota-owners must sign before a notary public in Egypt. Attach notarised passports, the name reservation certificate, registered-office lease consent, and an English translation of the Articles of Association authenticated by GAFI for foreign utilisation.
required_dossiers: Signed quota subscription schedule
Notarised passport / national ID copies of all shareholders
GAFI name reservation certificate
Registered office lease contract or landlord's written consent
Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
English translation of the Articles of Association for the GAFI file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary or GAFI legal counsel raises drafting issues, execute a corrective addendum to the Articles and re-notarise; GAFI re-review is completed within three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share capital deposit and bank escrow certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian commercial bank authorised by the Central Bank of Egypt, cooperating with GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation and draft Articles approval, open a temporary corporate account for the LLC under formation, deposit the declared share capital or the amount needed to satisfy the electrical contractor licence threshold, and request a bank certificate confirming the escrowed deposit addressed to GAFI. If capital is in-kind, obtain a certified valuation report and complete asset transfer documentation.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Preliminary Articles of Association draft
Shareholder resolution approving the subscribed capital
Passports / national IDs of the founders
Bank account application and capital remittance receipt
Certified in-kind valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines due to KYC deficiencies, submit corrected anti-money-laundering declarations. If escrow conditions are unusual, apply to the GAFI One-Stop-Shop for written facilitation to use another licensed Egyptian bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI incorporation submission and commercial registry entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop; Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade - Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation package through GAFI One-Stop-Shop, pay incorporation fees and stamp duties, and obtain the GAFI certificate of incorporation. Immediately after GAFI issuance, complete registration at the Commercial Registry to finalise the Egyptian juridical person's status and obtain the commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Notarised Articles of Association with all quota-owner signatures
Bank certificate evidencing escrowed share capital or in-kind valuation report
GAFI name reservation certificate
Pro-forma first board resolution
Registered office lease contract
GAFI incorporation certificate after issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or correction request, supply the requested attestations within ten business days. If the Commercial Registry requests fee reconciliation, pay at the registry treasury and resubmit on the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and provisional licensing consultation for high-voltage works
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Income and VAT registration desks; Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA) for contractor licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register with ETA for Tax Identification Number, tax card and VAT, and activate e-invoicing where required. Open operational bank accounts. In parallel, file the EgyptERA electrical contractor licence application and receive a provisional clearance before bidding on 500kV substation works.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial register extract
Articles of Association and board resolution appointing the legal representative
Registered office lease contract
Bank account details and share capital deposit proof
ETA registration forms and Egyptian contractor pre-qualification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA delays TIN issuance, escalate through the ETA investor complaints channel and obtain a temporary TIN acknowledgment. For EgyptERA delay, remedy by submitting the professional engineer certificates, insurance cover and financial solvency statements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA) for electrical contractor licensing; Industrial Development Authority (IDA) for any fixed operating or assembly facility; GAFI One-Stop-Shop for coordination of industrial licences.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Class A Electrical Contractor Licence for Extra-High-Voltage Substation Works / Industrial Operating Facility Licence where a fixed construction or assembly facility is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Environmental Impact Assessment Sector, Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Category B) where site works include substation foundations, transformer oil storage, SF6 gas handling and significant construction-phase impacts; simplified environmental registration where activities are limited to installation with no hazardous storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 48/1982 and Law No. 4/1994 as amended: zero discharge of transformer oil; wastewater effluent BOD no more than 60 mg/L, COD no more than 80 mg/L, TSS no more than 40 mg/L; SF6 leakage containment below 3% annual loss with recovery and inventory reporting; hazardous waste consignment to a licensed treatment facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Force fire-safety clearance for temporary site offices and laydown yards; structural survey or load approval for any substation building by a licensed structural engineer; Ministry of Labor Occupational Safety and Health clearance covering PPE, confined-space entry, working-at-height and high-voltage electrical safety procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) of the Ministry of Finance; digital services and registration portal for VAT, corporate income tax, e-invoicing and e-receipts at https://www.eta.gov.eg and https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity that carries on an economic activity in Egypt or is required to register for Egyptian VAT must apply for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) via the ETA's online taxpayer registration portal or by filing Form No. 1 with the competent ETA administrative office. The entity must submit the certified constitutional documents, a board resolution for the authorized representative, the commercial registration certificate if any, a valid foreign tax residency certificate, and a domestic address for service in Egypt. The ETA reviews the application and issues a unified tax card/TIN certificate; for VAT specifically, the entity must file the VAT registration application and, where the foreign entity has no permanent establishment in Egypt, the ETA may register the foreign principal with a designated Egyptian fiscal representative for VAT administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Egyptian resident LLC is subject to corporate income tax as an independent juridical person on worldwide income, while non-resident foreign entities are subject to Egyptian tax on Egyptian-source income only; no general territorial tax privilege applies outside free-zone or special-zone regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box entity classification election exists under Egyptian tax law; an LLC incorporated or effectively managed in Egypt is per se taxable as a corporation and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Certain statutory elections are available for corporate groups, such as loss offset elections within the group tax return rules, and the VAT regime permits ordinary deduction elections for input tax on mixed supplies. Foreign hybrid entities are evaluated under Egypt's tax-recharacterization principles for Egyptian treaty-tie-breaker purposes, and no proactive hybrid mismatch election is available absent a specific double-taxation agreement provision.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Egypt's Unified Tax Law framework and VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 and amendments
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and services; once exceeded, mandatory VAT registration is required; threshold applies to composite taxable turnover and excludes exempt supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a mandatory real-time e-invoicing and e-receipts clearance system administered by the ETA. All VAT-registered persons in the phased rollout must submit invoice and receipt data to the ETA portal in structured JSON/XML format, obtain a unique transaction UUID and encoded QR code, and integrate their accounting/ERP system with the ETA's application programming interface (API). Fiscal clearance is near-real-time: invoices undergo automated validation and digital stamping before issuance to the final customer; failure to clear invoices electronically can expose the supplier to administrative fines up to EGP 50,000 per non-compliant document and suspension of tax benefits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported by taxable persons are zero-rated if they are physically delivered outside Egypt and the export is accompanied by valid customs documentation proving actual departure within the statutory period. Services supplied to a non-resident customer who is outside Egypt and that are wholly or effectively consumed outside Egypt may be zero-rated, including offshore installation and commissioning services on infrastructure located outside Egypt; services directly related to immovable property located outside Egypt are generally outside Egyptian VAT or zero-rated. For all zero-rating claims the exporter must obtain and retain documents evidencing the supplier-customer relationship, the foreign destination, and the receipt of the invoice in hard currency through the Egyptian banking system.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to high audit scrutiny by the ETA and the Central Bank of Egypt. The tax authority may require production of the original export contract, invoices, customs declarations, payment evidence, and bank statements to establish that the exported goods or services actually left Egypt and that foreign currency proceeds were repatriated into Egypt. Fraudulent zero-rating or retrospective failure to repatriate proceeds results in reversal of the zero rate, assessment of avoided VAT, a delay penalty, and an additional monetary penalty of up to 100-200% of the tax evaded; criminal conviction for tax fraud may also carry imprisonment and debarment from exporting privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the unified monetary and exchange-control authority under the Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, acting with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) for currency-derivative market infrastructure and with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for registration of foreign capital into the EG_LLC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since March 2024 Egypt operates a flexible, market-determined exchange-rate regime in which EGP/USD and EGP/EUR rates are set on the interbank market and the CBE intervenes only to counter disorderly movements. Current-account transactions are freely convertible: payments for imported gas-insulated switchgear components, subcontractor services, royalties and trade settlements flow through licensed banks against invoice, contract and customs documentation without CBE prior licensing. Capital-account transactions, including non-resident equity injections, shareholder loans, disposal proceeds and profit remittances, are open but procedurally controlled: each flow is booked by the handling bank on the CBE electronic balance-of-payments platform with a Law 194/2020 purpose code, the underlying investment must be registered with GAFI, and the LLC must present audited financials, a tax clearance certificate and proof of the 10% dividend withholding tax (treaty-reduced where applicable) before the bank releases the transfer. The FX-arrears queue that existed before the floatation has been substantially cleared; residual hurdles are the market-driven volatility of the EGP, bank margins on FCY liquidity and the documentary strictness of purpose-code evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE rules on export receipts in force after the 2024 float, an Egyptian exporter must repatriate all export proceeds into the Egyptian banking system within statutory deadlines measured from shipment: generally 11 months for documentary letters of credit and 4 months for collection or negotiation instruments, with service-export receipts due within one year and longer periods available for construction and E&M contracts when certified project schedules are submitted. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to EGP: the EG_LLC may retain 100% of foreign-currency milestone receipts in a Foreign-Currency Account at its Egyptian bank and convert at the interbank rate when commercially attractive. Full repatriation and booking of the proceeds with the CBE Trade and FX monitoring system are mandatory; proceeds must not be held offshore, and for the 500 kV substation installation contracts each invoice must be supported by the owner's progress certificate matching the ISIC 4321 scope.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Operational Account + USD Foreign-Currency Account (GAFI-registered investment account for capital recording)
EGP Settlement Account + EUR/USD Foreign-Currency Accounts with trade-finance desk
EGP Settlement + USD FCA + LC issuing/confirmation and SWIFT MT103 corridor
Multi-currency FCA (EGP, USD, EUR, GBP) with global SWIFT mesh and treasury products
EGP + USD operational accounts and standby LC/performance bond desk
EGP + EUR/USD accounts for EPC contractors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW for treasury-critical flows. Egypt does not license offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) as banks; an offshore EMI cannot open a CBE-cleared EGP account, cannot issue local payment instruments and cannot produce the CBE purpose-code evidence needed for later profit repatriation. The EG_LLC may use a global business account only as an auxiliary reception channel for pre-contract deposits, provided the underlying contract is disclosed to the Egyptian bank and the balance is swept into Egypt by MT103; all subcontractor payments, customs duties, VAT, payroll and tax obligations must be executed through a licensed Egyptian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the market standard: Egyptian tier-1 banks require an in-person compliance interview at the account-opening branch for at least one board-authorized signatory and for each material UBO, under the AML Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Law No. 76 of 2016, the CBE AML rules and the Banking Law Art. 87. A purely remote opening for a foreign-owned de novo Egyptian LLC is not generally offered; acceptable alternatives are: (i) a notarized and apostilled (or Egyptian-consulate legalized) power of attorney from the non-resident directors to a resident Egyptian general manager who performs the physical interview with the original passports and corporate pack; or (ii) a hybrid process used by HSBC Egypt and CIB under which the corporate pack is submitted electronically, the Compliance Officer holds a mandatory video call with the UBOs, and the account mandate is physically signed at the branch thereafter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained multi-layer shareholding through a low-tax jurisdiction with undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificates of incorporation and registers of directors/members for each holding entity; a signed UBO declaration with passport copies and address proofs for all individuals holding more than 25%; a board resolution of EG_LLC describing the capital structure; and an ownership chart countersigned by the corporate service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity on the inbound capital injection, especially a lump-sum USD transfer from a remitting bank that is not the shareholder's habitual banker.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 of the injection; subscribed share agreement; shareholders' resolution approving the contribution; parent entity audited or management accounts demonstrating liquidity; GAFI capital registration receipt; and the notarized articles of association of the Egyptian LLC reflecting the paid-in capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags: milestone invoices not matching progress certificates, subcontract modifications exceeding 20% of the EPC value, or intra-group return flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original EPC contract with the owner/EETC; signed milestone acceptance and progress certificates; ISIC 4321-aligned packing and isolation lists for 500 kV gas-insulated switchgear components; POC accounting reports; and the Egyptian E-invoice codes of each milestone invoice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or adverse-media screening hits on a shareholder, director or beneficial owner, commonly where the local counterparty is a state-owned utility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit PEP status declaration; commercial rationale memorandum; source-of-wealth documentation including bank statements, investment statements and tax returns; enhanced CDD questionnaire executed by the identified person; and the tender award evidence from the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company or EETC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-integrated blocker: absence of a tax clearance file or unverified withholding-tax position that would freeze outbound FX remittances of profits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIT/VAT registration certificates; current tax clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority; e-invoiced milestone invoices; the LLC's payroll and social-insurance filing receipts; and the bank mandate proving that all supplier and payroll payments are executed to genuine third parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder wires USD or EUR by SWIFT MT103 to the EG_LLC Foreign-Currency Account at the chosen tier-1 Egyptian bank, with the beneficiary name matching exactly the Commercial Register entry and the payment details field citing 'Capital contribution - LLC - Shareholders resolution No. [...] dated [...] - GAFI file No. [...]'. The receiving bank verifies the CBE balance-of-payments purpose code for 'Direct investment - equity capital', credits the investment account and issues an inward remittance certificate. The LLC then updates the GAFI file and Commercial Register extract within the statutory window of approximately 30 days, after which the bank marks the investment as registered, enabling the statutory right of profit and liquidation remittance under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Shareholder loans must instead be routed under a written facility agreement with arm's-length interest, booked under the loan purpose code and respecting the 4:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor of the Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005; the inbound remittance must be clean principal without any withholding tax deduction, free of sanctions-flagged intermediaries, and sourced from a jurisdiction acceptable to the Egyptian bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails in priority order: (a) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for milestone progress payments to overseas subcontractors and equipment suppliers, each transfer carrying the correct CBE purpose code plus the proforma/commercial invoice reference and, for goods, the ACI Form 4 customs registration; (b) commercial letters of credit issued by the Egyptian bank (SWIFT MT700 with MT707 amendments) under UCP 600 for large GIS component imports, supported by the applicant's credit line, margin and conforming transport documents; (c) SWIFT MT760 standby letters of credit and bank guarantees for advance-payment, performance (typically 5-10% of contract value) and retention obligations toward the EETC or the private owner; (d) domestic EGP wires through the CBE RTGS (EG-RTGS) and Meeza Instant Payment System for local subcontractors, payroll and VAT settlements against E-invoice codes; (e) documentary collections (MT400) only for low-value repeat purchases. Since the March 2024 float, outbound FX payments are not CBE-licensed, but the bank executes them only on proof of the real economic transaction and may time the dispatch to its own interbank USD liquidity; the treasury must therefore maintain committed FX facilities and avoid accumulating large EGP positions between milestones.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracted by the EG_LLC with a licensed Egyptian bank, anchored to a genuine underlying USD/EGP receipt or import commitment, settled at the interbank reference rate at maturity and prohibited for speculative positions.
EGP/USD foreign-currency futures listed on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX derivatives segment) with central counterparty clearing and margin posting, used to hedge the EGP value of milestone receivables.

USD/EGP or EUR/EGP cross-currency swap with an Egyptian licensed dealer bank, matched to the maturity and interest profile of the LLC's FCY debt service or lumpy milestone receipts, supported by the underlying loan or contract documentation.
Interest-rate or commodity overlay swaps (ISDA master agreements) ancillary to the currency swap where the LLC finances imported 500 kV GIS components with SOFR-indexed credit.

Offshore synthetic non-deliverable forward (NDF) is permissible only at the level of the foreign parent as a hedge of its Egyptian equity exposure; the Egyptian resident EG_LLC may not transact offshore NDFs because that would breach CBE capital-control strictures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 20) together with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Corporate Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal year-end; 30 April for a 31 December tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to EGP 5,000, plus a monthly delayed-payment charge of 2% on the tax due; subsequent enforcement includes mandatory tax-card suspension, enforced collection, criminal prosecution for persistent non-filing, and listing as a non-compliant taxpayer in the ETA portal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (GAFI digital registry portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through January 31 each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EGP 100 per month of delay, suspension of the commercial registration certificate after 90 days, prohibition from tender participation and import/export clearance, and administrative strike-off after two consecutive years of non-renewal following a 60-day published notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) through the annual commercial-registry renewal form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each January commercial-registry renewal; within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or change in the UBO chain
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO data is punishable under Egyptian AML Law with fines and imprisonment; registry flagging, suspension of company transactions, and administrative strike-off upon repeated non-confirmation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size exemption. Companies Law 194/2020 requires every Egyptian LLC to appoint at least one auditor registered with the Financial Regulatory Authority at the General Assembly; annual audited financial statements must accompany the corporate income tax return and are a precondition to renewing the electrical installation license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as local GAAP, modeled on IFRS; IFRS as issued by IASB accepted for related consolidated reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: During the January commercial-registry renewal, the registered manager must verify the current register of members, certify all direct and indirect beneficial owners, and record any share transfers. Share transfers must be approved by the LLC managers/shareholders, entered in the statutory Register of Members on the transfer date, and filed with the Commercial Registry within 30 days; the updated UBO register must be available for EMLCU and GAFI inspection.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 900 per annum for a registered office or commercial agency in Cairo / Suez Canal Economic Zone, including legal-address service, mail handling, notarization, and GAFI portal maintenance.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 per annum for a licensed high-voltage substation installation LLC, depending on annual revenue, project sites, and number of audit visits.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% standard CIT rate under Law No. 91 of 2005 for all legal persons; oil and gas extraction subject to a separate 40.55% rate not applicable to ISIC 4321 electrical installation contractors
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 grants a deduction of up to 50% of investment costs for projects in underdeveloped governorates and in specified strategic sectors; newly established companies in certain economic zones may qualify for a 5-year tax holiday or reduced rates; a licensed project inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) may receive preferential CIT treatment of 10% if certified; this contractor would require a specific SCZone license to rely on the 10% rate and no incentive is assumed absent written ETA approval

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 17 (Legal Persons Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-TAX electronic portal at https://www.incometax.gov.eg; controlled transaction annexure Form TP-1 is submitted with the same annual filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return plus four quarterly advance CIT instalments (months 3, 6, 9 and 12 of the fiscal year) calculated on the previous year's liability and adjusted on the final return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form No. 17 must be filed within 4 months of the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end the filing deadline is 30 April of the following year; quarterly advance payments are payable within 30 days after quarter end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal person identification: taxpayer name, unified Tax Identification Number (TIN), commercial registration number, and ISIC activity code 4321
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Egyptian LLC's TIN and declare the foreign ownership percentage; attach the commercial registration and the power of attorney granted to the resident tax representative

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis and fiscal year period; applicable accounting standards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the calendar year unless prior ETA approval of a different period is evidenced; long-term installation contracts (500kV GIS substations) may be recognized under stage-of-completion only when certified completion reports are retained

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: contract milestone billings, installation, commissioning and related material supplies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report revenue gross of VAT (14%) and net of contractual retentions; reconcile each milestone to bank wire receipts and LC drawings; include any offshore-managed procurement fees recharged to the Egyptian entity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs: subcontract works, imported GIS equipment, salaries, equipment depreciation, GIL, insurance, bank charges, and site security
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all subcontractor invoices with valid Egyptian VAT registration numbers; related-party subcontracting must be justified by an arm's length TNMM or Cost Plus study and by actual staff and site presence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after statutory deductions and prior-year loss carryforward (maximum 5 years)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the loss utilization schedule; foreign branch losses outside Egypt are not deductible; losses of a disregarded offshore procurement vehicle may be reattributed to the LLC under the anti-avoidance rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Headline CIT at 22.5% on the taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advance instalments, stamp tax, and any foreign tax credits are then applied; a foreign tax credit is capped at the Egyptian tax attributable to the same foreign income and requires a legalized Tax Residency Certificate (TRC)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computations of net tax due, additional payment, or refund claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: ETA refunds are set off against any VAT or withholding tax exposures; refund review takes around 45 working days and requires independent audited financial statements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Controlled transaction disclosure: foreign related parties, transaction categories (services, subcontracting, financing, equipment leases), amounts in EGP, and the transfer pricing method selected
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory whenever any related-party transaction exists, regardless of value; use OECD-aligned CUP, TNMM or Profit Split; for intercompany engineering fees exceeding EGP 10 million, obtain a bilateral APA or informal ETA clearance before filing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: delay penalty equal to 2% per month or part of the tax due, capped at 150% of the tax; late payment: 2% monthly surcharge subject to the same cap; failure to file electronically: fixed administrative fine of EGP 1,000 to 5,000; false or incomplete TP disclosure: penalty of 30% of the additional tax resulting from a later transfer pricing adjustment; criminal penalties of imprisonment and fines apply to knowingly false declarations

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends and profit distributions made by the LLC to non-resident shareholders; dividends paid to resident Egyptian corporate shareholders are generally exempt; distributions in kind by foreign-controlled LLCs are equally subject to the 10% WHT on fair market value
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Obtain from the tax authority of the recipient's fiscal domicile a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) covering the dividend payment date; 2) submit to the ETA a Form WT-2 treaty reduction application attaching the TRC, the LLC shareholding register, and the applicable double tax agreement (DTA); 3) the ETA issues an approval for the reduced withholding rate, typically within 30 to 60 days; 4) apply the reduced DTA rate (commonly 5% to 15% for substantial shareholdings) on the next distribution, or claim a refund of excess withholding under Article 52 of Law 91 of 2005; advance application is mandatory to avoid the default 10% withholding
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 20% on royalties and technical/service fees paid to non-residents and 20% on interest paid to non-residents (Law 91 of 2005 as amended); typical DTA reductions: royalties 10% to 15%, interest 10% to 15% depending on the treaty partner; interest on foreign bank loans concluded under Central Bank of Egypt approval may be fully exempt if the loan agreement and drawdown notice are filed with the ETA; royalty characterization of software and engineering licences is narrowly applied in Egypt and must be supported by an IP ownership and licence fee audit

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when the aggregate value of controlled transactions of the Egyptian LLC equals or exceeds EGP 10 million per fiscal year; Master File: mandatory when the multinational enterprise group's consolidated worldwide turnover equals or exceeds EGP 1 billion; Form TP-1 remains mandatory for every taxpayer with any controlled transaction, even below the EGP 10 million threshold; documentation, if not maintained, triggers a 30% penalty on the tax adjustment and shifts the burden of proof to the taxpayer
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not have a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) law as in the UAE, but the ETA applies a general anti-avoidance rule and the substance-over-form doctrine under Law No. 91 of 2005; the LLC must maintain verifiable Egyptian substance: leased or owned head office, Egyptian payroll, site staff and engineers, equipment inventory, bank accounts, and a 500kV electrical installation license from the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company; a letterbox entity with offshore management and no local operational activity will be disregarded, may lose treaty benefits, and can be assessed on the total contract value rather than on a service fee basis; under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 the company must commence actual activity within six months of licensing or face cancellation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing subcontract milestone revenues, issuing or accepting fictitious engineering invoices, overstating imported equipment costs, or creating artificial subcontracting chains for high-voltage GIS installation works
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment from 3 to 5 years and a fine between EGP 10,000 and 50,000, plus payment of double the evaded tax; 48-hour bank account freeze and seizure of project equipment; the ETA reopens all affected years and imposes the 150% cap on monthly delay penalties; debarment from tenders for state electricity projects
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the fines, evaded tax and penalties through piercing of the corporate veil; the Economic Court may impose a travel ban and asset seizure order; board members and the signatory tax agent face criminal prosecution and a 5-year ban on holding office in any Egyptian commercial company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC is used solely to sign the Egyptian contract while all project execution, invoicing, staffing, insurance and bank financing are performed by the parent company offshore; no Egyptian office, no resident engineers, no substation equipment and no operational licence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the commercial registration and investment licence; denial of Article 21 recognition; recharacterization of the LLC as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent; assessment of 22.5% CIT on the full contract proceeds plus 2% monthly late penalties (capped at 150%); automatic refusal of the SCZone or treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the foreign parent are jointly liable for all unassessed taxes, penalties and interest; the travel ban regime applies to all shareholders and signatories; personal bank accounts holding project receivables are subject to seizure; the responsible officers may be prosecuted for operating an unlicensed electrical installation business

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Egyptian LLC earns a residual profit margin below 2% while the foreign parent charges excessive management fees, procurement margins, software licence and equipment rental fees; intercompany loans carry interest above commercial bank rates or exceed Egyptian thin capitalization limits; Form TP-1 is omitted or documents indicate an unapproved profit split
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA makes a transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's length profit margin under OECD-aligned rules; additional CIT of 22.5% on the adjusted profit; monthly delay penalty of 2% up to 150% of the additional tax; if the TP file is missing, an automatic penalty equal to 30% of the adjustment is imposed; the entire intercompany interest and royalty deduction may be disallowed
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The finance director and tax manager are personally liable for the additional tax up to the amount of the unjust enrichment; the Economic Court may freeze personal accounts and property where funds were transferred to the parent during the audited period; directors may be prohibited from leaving Egypt until the full assessment is paid or secured

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Failure to Withhold
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Project milestone payments are directed to personal bank accounts; subcontractors are settled in cash above the statutory threshold; circular letters of credit are used between the LLC and offshore sister companies; the LLC fails to withhold 20% tax on engineering royalties and 20% tax on interest remitted to non-residents and fails to file quarterly WHT returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, imprisonment from 3 to 7 years and a fine between EGP 100,000 and 1,000,000, with confiscation of the funds laundered; the ETA separately assesses the unwithheld tax as a liability of the LLC, plus the 2% monthly delay penalty; VAT penalties of 20% of the unpaid VAT and 2% monthly interest are automatically added; bank accounts and LC margins are frozen for the duration of the investigation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted withholding taxes and AML fines; personal travel bans and seizure orders are routinely issued by the Economic Court; the compliance officer faces independent criminal liability for failing to report suspicious transactions to the Egyptian Money Laundering Combat Unit (EMLCU); the parent company's board may be prosecuted under the joint control doctrine where cash flows were visibly diverted
